title: Cross-Modal Evidence Playbook for Model-Serving Compliance
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Purpose:
This playbook documents a pragmatic, auditable workflow for collecting, validating, and delivering security and compliance evidence spanning RBAC/authorization artifacts, immutable audit streams, data residency and retention proofs, Secure SDLC outputs, incident-forensic captures, and exception records for Redwood model-serving platforms. It is intended to be actionable for security engineers, SREs, and compliance reviewers.

Applicability and boundaries:
- Applies to: hosted API, Dedicated, and Private model-serving deployments.
- In-scope artifacts: role/policy snapshots, entitlement change logs, audit stream extracts, storage/residency manifests, CI/CD build attestations, signed release manifests, forensic captures, and exception approvals.
- Out-of-scope: commercial contracts, external vendor financials.

High-level objectives and metrics:
- Deliver audit-ready evidence bundles for routine requests within 48 hours; for urgent regulatory demands, target 24 hours.
- Maintain cryptographic integrity checks for all ingested artifacts.
- Preserve provenance metadata (collector identity, collection timestamp, verification status, storage location, legal hold flag).

Ownership and contact points:
- Evidence Orchestration: security-platform team (primary)
- RBAC Authoritative Source: Identity & Access team
- Audit Stream Management: Observability team
- SDLC Artifact Custody: Eng-DevEx and Build Reliability
- Incident Forensics: Eng-SRE and Incident Response
- Legal/Compliance Review: security-compliance team

Artifact inventory (summary entries):
- RBAC snapshots: policy exports, role definitions, role bindings.
- Entitlement change logs: principal-role assignment history with session ids.
- Immutable audit extracts: compressed, sequenced log slices with sequence checksums.
- Residency proofs: deployment manifests showing data store locations and encryption domains.
- Retention metadata: retention class, expiry timestamps, and legal hold markers.
- SDLC artifacts: signed build manifest, test matrix, code-review snapshots.
- Forensic captures: node state, container snapshots, memory dump indexes.
- Exception records: approval ticket, compensating controls, expiry.

Minimum metadata required per artifact (must be present on ingest):
- artifact_id: stable locator string created by the collector
- artifact_type: short tag (rbac, audit-snapshot, residency-manifest, build-manifest, forensic-capture, exception)
- collected_by: service principal or user
- collected_ts: ISO8601 timestamp
- storage_uri: canonical storage location
- integrity_hash: SHA256 (hex)
- verification_status: pending | verified | failed
- region_tag: region or global

Ingest workflow (automated):
1) Collector services run on schedule or on-demand and write artifacts to immutable object storage.
2) Collector calls evidence ingest endpoint with a manifest payload containing the minimum metadata.
3) Evidence orchestration validates signature and integrity_hash, annotates chain-of-custody, and indexes the manifest in the evidence catalog.
4) If verification fails, orchestration marks the artifact with verification_status=failed and triggers the collector retry DAG.

Example ingest CLI (illustrative):
- collector: rbac-exporter --tenant-id T123 --out s3://evidence/rbac/T123/policy-2029-02-01.json --sha256 abc123 --collected-by rbac-exporter-1
- ingest: curl -X POST https://evidence.redwood.internal/v1/ingest -d "manifest_uri=s3://evidence/rbac/T123/policy-2029-02-01.manifest&artifact_type=rbac&collected_by=rbac-exporter-1&collected_ts=2029-02-01T14:32:00Z&integrity_hash=abc123"

Validation and integrity rules:
- All artifacts must provide an integrity_hash; ingestion refuses artifacts without one.
- The orchestration service will re-calculate the hash against the stored object before marking verified.
- Collector principals must use rotating service keys with automated key rotation audits.

Data residency and retention mapping:
- Residency manifests must include deployment_id, data_domains, storage_regions, and kms_key_id for encrypted stores.
- Default retention tiers: HOT (0-90d), WARM (90d-2y), COLD (2y-7y), ARCHIVE (7y+).
- For EEA personal data, artifacts must be stored in eu-* buckets with EU-KMS keys. The residency manifest must explicitly assert the jurisdictional constraint.

Legal hold and immutable flagging:
- Any incident marked regulatory or litigation sets legal_hold=true for associated artifacts.
- Deletion/expiry jobs must skip artifacts with legal_hold=true; compliance will clear holds only after written approval.

Incident evidence capture steps (operational runbook):
1) Incident owner declares evidence scope in the incident ticket and assigns evidence_criticality.
2) For high/regulatory incidents, run the forensic capture sequence: export current RBAC for affected tenants, snapshot audit streams for the relevant time window, capture container and node runtime state, and collect related SDLC release manifests.
3) Upload artifacts to evidence store and run ingest flow for each artifact.
4) Apply legal hold if the incident is regulatory; mark artifacts immutable in the evidence catalog.
5) Security-compliance performs review and records any redactions and redaction provenance.

Exception management pattern:
- Exceptions must be created with clear scope, owner, compensating controls, and expiry date.
- Store exception evidence under a dedicated exception folder and set retention to expiry + 3 years.
- Automated notifications: owners receive reminders 30, 7, and 1 day before expiry.

Packaging audit bundles and delivery options:
- Bundles include: a human-readable index, signed manifest, artifact links, cryptographic checksums, and a control-to-artifact mapping.
- Delivery methods: encrypted S3 share (time-limited credentials), secure SFTP, or physically sealed media for restricted external requests.
- Packaging CLI example: redwood-evidence package --control-ids SOC2-6,SOC2-7 --from 2029-01-01 --to 2029-01-31 --out /tmp/bundle-202901.tar.gz

Search and queries (examples):
- Find artifacts for incident: search evidence catalog for incident_id:INC-2029-0456
- Find unverified artifacts older than 24h: search for verification_status:pending AND collected_ts < now-24h

Operational runbooks (links and summary):
- Ingest failure: check collector logs, re-run collector with replay window, escalate to Observability oncall if repeated failures.
- Integrity mismatch: quarantine artifact, trigger collector replay, notify Legal if bundle already delivered externally.
- Residency discrepancy: run residency-proof generator and attach generated manifest to the affected bundle.

Audit readiness checklist (pre-delivery):
- All required manifests are present and verification_status is verified.
- Chain-of-custody entries present for each artifact.
- Residency manifest aligns with storage URI and kms_key_id.
- Any redactions are recorded with provenance and original checksum retained under legal hold.
- Exception approvals included in the bundle.

Rollout and validation plan:
- Canary (30 days): enable ingestion for RBAC and audit snapshots in a single region; validate end-to-end ingest and verification.
- Regional expansion (60 days): enable residency and retention manifests and legal-hold flows across regions.
- Full integration (90 days): onboard SDLC and forensic captures; execute a simulated regulator audit with Legal and Compliance.

Appendix: sample manifest line (textual, not machine parsed):
artifact_id: rbac-T123-20290201-1  | artifact_type: rbac  | collected_by: rbac-exporter-1  | collected_ts: 2029-02-01T14:32:00Z  | storage_uri: s3://evidence/rbac/T123/policy-2029-02-01.json  | integrity_hash: abc123  | verification_status: verified

Key integrations and references:
- evidence-orchestration service repository: github.com/redwood/security-evidence
- Orchestrator DAGs: airflow-redwood-security (rbac-exporter, audit-snapshotter, build-harvester, forensic-agent)
- Evidence catalog: elastic index obs-evidence-prod with read-only backups in s3://evidence-catalog-backups
- Immutable storage: s3://evidence-immutable with WORM where required

Contacts and escalation:
- Evidence orchestration oncall: security-platform@redwood.ai (PagerDuty: SEC-EVIDENCE)
- Legal/compliance team: security-compliance@redwood.ai

Revision log:
- 2029-03-01: Created by Jordan Patel.
- 2029-03-07: Added residency mapping and legal hold guidance (review: Arielle Kim).
- 2029-03-12: Finalized incident capture steps and packaging examples (review: Noah Martinez).

End of playbook.
